headlines: MIAMI-DADE APPROVES $1.02 MILLION INCENTIVE FOR MIAMI VICE MOVIE
NEW MIAMI VICE FILM BRINGS JOBS AND SPENDING HOME
MIAMI VICE RETURNS WITH MILLIONS PROMISED FOR LOCAL WORKERS
draft.article:
Miami-Dade County commissioners approved a $1.02 million production incentive package Tuesday to help fund the upcoming film Miami Vice '85. The movie will star Austin Butler as Sonny Crockett and Michael B. Jordan as Ricardo Tubbs, directed by Joseph Kosinski.

To secure the single reimbursement payment, filmmakers must invest heavily in the community. Requirements include spending at least $10 million in Miami-Dade County, hiring county residents for 30 percent or more of the below-the-line local crew, and setting up county production offices.

Additionally, the team must use local studios and allocate at least half of vendor spending, or $5 million, to area businesses. The movie hits theaters in May 2028.

headlines: FOUR DISPLACED AND CAT DIES IN NW MIAMI-DADE FIRE
EARLY MORNING DUPLEX FIRE IN NORTHWEST MIAMI-DADE
MIAMI CREWS STOP FAST DUPLEX BLAZE IN TEN MINUTES
draft.article: Miami Fire Rescue responded to an early morning duplex fire on Wednesday in Northwest Miami-Dade, leaving four residents without a home. First responders arrived at 1437 NW 50th Street at 5:37 a.m. after receiving reports of the blaze. Crews quickly deployed hose lines to battle the flames while additional personnel searched the inside of the duplex for any remaining occupants. Firefighters managed to bring the fire under control within 10 minutes of their arrival. Four people and one dog survived the incident and were displaced from the property. Officials confirmed that the family cat died in the fire.

headlines: TERRA SECURES $507M LOAN FOR 28 STORY MIAMI BEACH TOWER
A $507 MILLION WATERFRONT TOWER REACHES WEST AVENUE
A MASSIVE NEW BAYFRONT CONDO IS COMING TO MIAMI BEACH
draft.article:
Miami Beach is set for a major new bayfront tower as Terra and partners RG Development Group, GV Development, and LORE Development secure a $507 million construction loan from TYKO Capital. The financing moves forward a planned 28-story luxury condominium at 1250 West Avenue.

Rising along Biscayne Bay on the western shoreline of Miami Beach, the development will feature 106 residences with views of the bay and Miami skyline. Plans include ground-floor retail, underground parking, a spa, a padel court, and pools on both the ground level and rooftop, plus two penthouses with private rooftop pools. Sales begin in 2027.

The project also brings public realm upgrades, including enhancements to the local Baywalk to expand pedestrian waterfront access.

headlines: INFINITY COLLECTIVE REVISES ALTON ROAD MIXED USE DEVELOPMENT PLANS
NEW MIAMI BEACH TOWER PLANS UNVEILED
CHANGES AHEAD FOR THE FORMER MIAMI BEACH EPICURE SITE
draft.article: Plans are shifting for the prominent vacant lot where the Epicure Gourmet Market once operated in Miami Beach. New York-based developer Infinity Collective is bringing updated plans to the Miami Beach Planning Board on Dec. 8 for the 1.4-acre site between 1656 and 1680 Alton Road, right next to Lincoln Road. The revised design by PBDW Architects cuts 38 rental apartments to bring the total to 142 units inside the 14-story, 302,135-square-foot building. It also boosts Class A office space to 51,200 square feet and expands ground-level retail to 45,313 square feet. A companion five-story garage with around 365 parking stalls is slated across the block at 1677 West Avenue.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE COUNTY TARGETS 2,000 CERTIFIED SMALL BUSINESSES BY 2027
MORE LOCAL FIRMS LAND MIAMI-DADE CONTRACTS
HOW 1,732 LOCAL BUSINESSES ACCESS BILLIONS IN MIAMI CONTRACTS
draft.article: Miami-Dade County currently has 1,732 certified small firms competing for public contracts, with officials aiming to reach 2,000 certified businesses by 2027. Through the county's Small Business Development programs, local enterprises can obtain Small Business Enterprise certifications in construction, architectural and engineering, or goods and services. Federal certifications like DBE and ACDBE are also available. County staff provide online application support, individual technical assistance, and training to navigate public procurement. Certified companies gain access to bid preferences, subcontractor goals, and set-asides. These county certifications are also recognized by partners such as Jackson Health System, Dade County Public Schools, and the City of Miami, unlocking billions in contracting opportunities.

headlines: COUNTY ADVANCES $100 MILLION PLAN TO REDEVELOP SHUTTERED SEAQUARIUM
NEW MARINA PROPOSED FOR MIAMI SEAQUARIUM
WHAT WILL HAPPEN TO OUR ICONIC MIAMI SEAQUARIUM SITE
draft.article:
Miami-Dade commissioners voted unanimously on Tuesday to advance a 100 million dollar redevelopment proposal for the shuttered Seaquarium site. The county-owned, 38-acre waterfront property closed down last year following an eviction battle centered on animal-welfare concerns.

Developer David Martin of Terra plans to lease the land for 99 years, keeping the Seaquarium name while building an aquarium, public baywalk, restaurants, event venues, a 325-slip marina, and drydock storage for over 500 boats.

Environmental advocates urged officials to delay the action. Rachel Silverstein of Miami Waterkeeper raised alarms over water quality, coral, and seagrass damage. Martin stated his design reduces environmental impact on Biscayne Bay. A final commission vote is expected by the end of the year.

headlines: DOLPHINS DEFENSE SECURES FIRST FUMBLE RECOVERY OF THE SEASON
DRILLS PAY OFF FOR MIAMI DEFENSE
CAN AGGRESSIVE DEFENSIVE PUNCHES SPARK MIAMI'S FIRST WIN
draft.article:
Miami Gardens saw months of defensive drills pay off during the Dolphins' recent matchup against Cincinnati. In the second quarter, rookie cornerback Chris Johnson punched the football loose from Bengals running back Chase Brown inside the ten-yard line. Defensive end Josh Uche secured the loose ball following an initial recovery by Chop Robinson.

The takeaway marked Miami's first fumble recovery of the season. Head coach Jeff Hafley has stressed ball-punching techniques since May organized team activities to generate game-changing momentum.

The 0-5 Dolphins now look to carry this defensive focus on the road against the 2-4 New York Jets on Sunday as they battle for their first victory.

headlines: NICK RICHARDS SECURES FULL CONTRACT GUARANTEE WITH MIAMI HEAT

HEAT LOCK IN VETERAN BIG MAN AHEAD OF OPENER
draft.article: Nick Richards officially secured his roster spot with the Miami Heat early Wednesday ahead of the team's season opener against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Kaseya Center. The 11:59 p.m. Tuesday deadline passed without a waiver, guaranteeing the 28-year-old veteran's full $3,066,143 salary for the season. Richards counts for $2,449,421 against Miami's salary cap and hard cap. The Heat continue managing strict financial room following the offseason acquisition of Giannis Antetokounmpo, carrying 14 players on standard contracts. Head coach Erik Spoelstra praised the conditioning of the 6-foot-11 big man, who provides frontcourt depth alongside Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo, and Bobby Portis.

The year 1906 was when these waterways were first initiated in the region. The canals were begun specifically to carry out the process of removing water from the Everglades.
